title: Embeddings & Reranking: unit-price model with decaying batch discounts and enterprise QSA alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: As usage of embeddings and reranking products grows, customers report unpredictable per-request costs (large batch requests + high dimensionality). We need a simple, predictable per-vector unit economics model and an opinionated batch discount curve that preserves gross margin while increasing adoption for high-throughput customers. This ticket defines the experiment and enterprise contract / security questionnaire (QSA) implications for the new pricing approach.

Problem statement: Current billing (per-request / per-GB) obscures unit economics for embeddings and reranking. Large batch inference (e.g., embeddinging 10M vectors) can generate bill shock and negotiation friction in enterprise SOWs. Sales and Finance request an audited unit price model and an automated batch discount schedule to streamline quotes and reduce custom discounting.

Proposed model (high level):
- Base unit: 1 vector embedding = 1 unit (regardless of dimensionality up to pre-specified limits). For models with > 2K dims, apply a dimensionality multiplier (see technical appendix link).
- Reranking: charge per query-rank pair as a single unit (e.g., ranking N candidates for 1 query = N units). Offer a small per-operation uplift for contextual rerank (when additional tokens are supplied).
- Batch discounts: decaying volume tiers applied monthly per-customer: Tier A 1-10k units = x price, Tier B 10k-1M units = x*0.7, Tier C 1M-10M = x*0.45, Tier D 10M+ = x*0.30. Add a runway for negotiated enterprise commitments that can override the public curve.
- Free tier: first 50k units cumulative across embeddings+rerank per month for new signups (to encourage experimentation).

Why this design: unit pricing clarifies seller conversations, aligns with usage patterns (vector-level costs dominate compute), and allows simple volume-based discounts that are easy to communicate in contract exhibits.

Open questions to resolve in experiment:
1) Exact baseline price per unit (financial modeling required).
2) Dimensionality multiplier thresholds and caps.
3) Rerank contextual token surcharge amount.
4) How to represent bundled usage (e.g., embeddings + similarity search included in a single unit calculation).

Deliverables: PRD + release notes, billing implementation (metering + invoice line item), SDK changes to surface batch estimator, public pricing page update, enterprise contract exhibit template, QSA answers for security questionnaire updates.
success_metrics: 1) 10% increase in paid volume from high-throughput customers within 90 days. 2) < 15% churn from customers in top 50 accounts on rollout. 3) 50% reduction in custom discount paperwork for embeddings/reranking quotes. 4) No revenue regression across top-10 accounts vs baseline (±5%).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Research, Feb 10 - Feb 28): gather finance/eng/ops inputs, sizing model, legal QSA gaps. Owner: Aisha. Phase 1 (Experiment launch, Mar 8 - Mar 31): release discounted unit pricing as an experiment for 25% of new signups and opt-in for existing customers via billing preview. Track revenue, conversion, and billing errors. Owner: Thomas + ENG billing team. Phase 2 (Enterprise contract & QSA, Mar 20 - Apr 10): prepare contract exhibit template and update security questionnaire answers; Legal & Security sign-off required before GA enterprise offers. Phase 3 (GA rollout, target Apr 15): full public pricing page update, SDK billing estimator, migration path for existing customers. Communication: blog post, changelog, customer success outreach, sales playbook.
technical_requirements: - Billing meter: ability to record 'vector_unit' and 'rerank_unit' with dimensionality tag. - Aggregation: monthly per-customer aggregation pipeline with tiered multiplier. - Pricing engine: support decaying tier price curve and enterprise overrides. - Invoices: new invoice line items and export mapping to accounting ledger. - SDK: client-side batch cost estimator + warning when crossing tiers. - Backcompat: existing customers get an opt-in preview and a 90-day notice before mandatory migration. - Observability: dashboards for daily unit ingestion, revenue by tier, and top customers at risk. ENG ticket to implement: ENG-3892 (metering) and ENG-3920 (billing engine).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Large customers may game the dimensionality multiplier by downsampling vectors — mitigate by threshold caps and usage policy. Risk: Metering errors could under/over-bill — mitigate with canary rollout, synthetic traffic verification jobs, and invoice reconciliation scripts. Risk: Enterprise legal asks for custom discounts outside the public curve — mitigate by publishing an explicit negotiation band and centralizing approvals in Finance. Security/QSA risk: adding new invoice metadata may require review of PII handling; Legal & Security to sign off before GA.
